_note: SPAWN AND EXIT BADGES, PLACED FROM LANE GEOMETRY. Nothing here names a level or a coordinate: systems/Markers.ts walks every lane in the level's own map and puts a spawn badge on the first waypoint of every lane an enemy can enter from and an exit badge on the last waypoint of every lane that runs to an exit. Re-tracing a plate moves them; adding a level adds them. The four numbers below are the only things authored.
_badgeScreenWidth: THE BADGE IS 40 CSS PIXELS ACROSS AT DEFAULT ZOOM, which is the unit it was asked for in and the only one that means anything for a thing you look at. The WORLD width falls out of it -- 40 / camera.defaultZoom -- exactly as buildPad.quietScreenWidth does, so changing the zoom band does not silently resize the badge. Deriving it the other way round, from a hardcoded world size, is what makes a prop that is the right size on a desktop and wrong on a phone.
_arrowOffset: THE ARROW'S CENTRE SITS 0.736 x THE BADGE'S RENDERED WIDTH from the badge's centre, along the lane's direction of travel. At rotation 0 that reproduces the original render exactly, which is where the number comes from -- it is a measurement of how the two pieces were drawn together, not a taste. It is a fraction of the RENDERED width rather than a pixel count so it survives the badge being resized.
_alpha: 0.7 SINCE 2026-09-14, down from 1.0. The note this replaces said the number existed to be turned down later without a re-render once the badges read as clutter, and that is exactly what live play reported -- they were the loudest thing on the board. 0.7 is the brief's value and it holds on every plate including the busiest: level 9 and level 10 are dark machine boards and the badges are light, so contrast carries them at 0.7 with room to spare; level 1's village is the brightest plate and the badge still reads as furniture against grass. Shipping at 1.0 was deliberate -- a prop that arrives already faded cannot be judged -- and it has now been judged. MEASURED, 844x390, badge luma against the plate beside it: level 6 reads 80, level 8 94, level 9 84, level 1 51, level 10 49 -- and LEVEL 7 IS THE WORST PLATE AT ABOUT 9 ON ALL SIX OF ITS BADGES, with level 4's upper spawn at 8.5. That is NOT an alpha problem and raising the number does not fix it: alpha blends toward the plate, so contrast scales linearly with it and 1.0 would take level 7 from 9.2 to 13.1, which is still nothing. The Highway is dark asphalt and the badge art is dark, so the two are the same luminance; separating them is a light halo or a darker outline in the PICTURE. Left at 0.7 and recorded as an art item in reports/2026-09-14-ui-cleanup.md.
_mergeWithin: HOW CLOSE TWO MARKERS OF THE SAME KIND HAVE TO BE, IN BADGE WIDTHS, BEFORE ONLY ONE IS DRAWN. Level 8's two exits are 437 px apart and both get one; level 9's two entrance lanes SHARE a painted mouth and start at the same point, so without this they would draw two badges exactly on top of each other and the overlap would read as a rendering fault. 1.0 badge width is the smallest threshold that cannot fire on two markers a player would read as separate. AND THE INSET DOES NOT BREAK IT: level 9's two entrance lanes share a painted mouth and are traced from the same point, so walking both 140 px in along their own lanes keeps them within a badge width of each other and they still draw as ONE badge -- measured at 6.0, where the marker count is 32 and not 33. It stops being one at about 8 badge widths, where the two arms have diverged far enough to be two; that is another reason not to inset further than the measurement asks for.
_insetBadgeWidths: HOW FAR ALONG ITS OWN LANE A BADGE SITS FROM THE LANE'S TERMINAL WAYPOINT, IN BADGE WIDTHS, toward the middle of the map. 6.0 badge widths is 140 world px at the shipped badge size, and it is MEASURED rather than chosen: 5.871 is the smallest value at which the whole badge AND its rotated arrow sit inside the 1280x720 plate on all 32 markers across all ten levels, and 6.0 is the first clean value above it. Below 5.5 there are markers hanging off the frame -- at 0 there are 15 of them, worst 10.6 px, and 27 of the 32 are being rescued by clampToPlate instead. At 6.0 nothing is outside and clampToPlate fires on nothing at all, which is the point: the inset does the work and the clamp is a backstop rather than the mechanism. IN BADGE WIDTHS, NOT PIXELS, for the reason arrowOffset is: the badge is specified by its screen width and a pixel inset would silently stop being enough the moment badgeScreenWidth moved. IT APPLIES ONLY TO A TERMINAL THAT IS OFF THE PLATE, which is every gateway point and is the whole of the fault; level 9's door at (1177, 329) is an exit INSIDE the plate and does not move, because the badge there means 'they get out HERE' and walking it 140 px up the road would point it at a piece of lane that is not the exit. See systems/Markers.ts and reports/2026-09-14-ui-cleanup.md.
